status: registered in REGISTRY.md section 14; held for ratification with -01
digest_rule: composed_digest = lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 RFC 8785 (JCS) serialization of the digest input object (CPB canonicalization algorithm 'jcs'); see canonical_preimage in each case.
envelope_profile: AAC Producer Envelope: tagged COSE_Sign1, protected {1: -8, 3: 'application/agent-action-capsule-id', 4: raw Ed25519 public key}, empty unprotected map, attached payload = raw 32-byte capsule_id.

cases.description: Two responders granted an Evidence Bundle each. Both root records carry the pre-agreed exchange identifier and the same transcript digest, so the join derives agree. The observers declare different custody domains and the records carry different keys, so the agreement is reported as corroborating (on declared custody).

The agree composition with responder-b's Evidence Bundle not carried and declared in missing. The composed digest is identical to the agree case: it covers member digests, outcomes, observers and join declarations, never member bodies. Composition closure is withheld (declared incomplete), not failed; the join is declared but cannot be re-derived, and no corroboration is reported.

A runtime observer and a network-boundary observer agree on one egress, but both observers declare the same custody domain. Different signing keys do not change that. The join derives agree; the verifier reports the pair as redundant, not corroborating.

The agree composition, with responder-a carrying its response envelope without the artifact bytes: its request_digest is the member's and its artifact_digest is the member's bundle digest. The envelope is outside the composed digest, so the digest is the agree case's. The envelope carries no signature in any deployment profile, so it is reported signature_unverified (withheld), as a refusal's signature would be.

As artifact-response-bound, but the envelope's request_digest is the digest of another request (the one responder-b answered): the artifact is bound to a request other than its member's, and the block fails.

The agree composition, with every Bundle checkpointed. Each member Bundle is its responder's whole log (one record): a completeness certificate over seq 1..1 and the log's first checkpoint, signed as a COSE statement by the responder's key. The container is the composer's whole log, checkpointed the same way under the composer's key. Every claim of the container and of each member passes, so the strict verdict of each is VALID, and with the block passing the full verdict is VALID. The member digests cover the certificates and checkpoints, so the composed digest is not the agree case's.
